subject: CatalystData trial: prompt & log handoff + evaluation playbook
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@catalystdata.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: CatalystData trial: prompt & log handoff + evaluation playbook

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap + next steps so we have the plan captured: 

Summary of the call:
- Goal: Validate Redwood's retrieval-augmented generation flow on CatalystData's customer support logs and the new FAQ assistant.
- POC scope: 2-week ingestion + 1-week evaluation; target evaluating quality (answer correctness & hallucination rate) and 95th-pctl latency under load.

Mutual action items (what we need from CatalystData):
1) Prompt set: 400–800 representative user prompts (CSV), prioritized by frequency. Include: id, user_query, prior_context (optional), expected_response (if available), use_case_tag.
2) Raw logs: 1–2 weeks of anonymized support chat transcripts (up to ~50k tokens total). If you can't provide full logs, a sampled set with session IDs is fine.
3) Success criteria: a short list (3 metrics) you want us to validate against (e.g., >85% correct, <10% irrelevant answers, avg latency <250ms).
4) SFTP or S3 transfer method and point-of-contact for secure handoff.

What Redwood will deliver:
- Evaluation plan and rubric (we attached a draft: redwood_eval_plan.md).
- A pass/fail summary against your success criteria + detailed error categories and example failing prompts.
- Suggested model/quantization profile and cost estimate for production.

Proposed timeline:
- CatalystData delivers prompt CSV + logs by EOD Thu, Jun 24 (10 business days from today).
- Redwood completes ingest + run of eval within 7 business days after receipt (report due Mon, Jul 5).

Attachments: catalyst_prompt_template.csv (sample columns), redwood_eval_plan.md (draft), s3_transfer_instructions.pdf (secure upload options).

Can you confirm the handoff timeline and whether the S3 presign or SFTP is preferable? If you need more time, propose a date and we'll adjust.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Prompt set: we can deliver ~500 logged user queries exported from the product. Can you confirm the CSV column order you prefer? (id, query, context, expected_response, tags?)
- Logs: we need to run a PII scrub first. Our security team estimated 48–72 hours. Is that okay?
- Success criteria: we'll draft 3 metrics but want Redwood to propose defaults if we don't decide in time.

We prefer S3 presigned URLs for the upload (easier for our data engineering team). Point of contact: Darin Li (data-pipeline@catalystdata.com).

We can target delivery on Fri, Jun 25 EOD after the scrub. If Redwood needs the sample earlier, we can send a small 50-query sample by Wed morning for initial checks.

Best — Olivia

Hi Olivia — quick technical notes / checklist for the CSV and logs to avoid hiccups on ingest: 

CSV checklist (columns must match template):
- id (string, unique)
- user_query (UTF-8, no line breaks inside cells recommended)
- prior_context (optional JSON blob or short text)
- expected_response (optional but very helpful for exact-match checks)
- priority (high/med/low)
- tag (product_area)

Logs checklist:
- Remove direct PII (names, emails). Replace with stable pseudonyms where possible.
- Provide a small manifest CSV mapping sample file names to session IDs and date ranges.
- If encrypted, share decryption/keys via Darin's secure channel; otherwise we provide presigned S3 buckets.

Transfer options (we prefer presigned S3):
- We'll create a time-limited, write-only presigned URL and share it with Darin. Look for an email from uploads@redwood.com with the subject "Redwood S3 upload: CatalystData".
- If SFTP is absolutely necessary, let us know and we will provide connection details and a temporary account.

Privacy/contract note: We will not retain raw logs beyond the evaluation unless you opt into retention; retention options are in the attached eval plan.

I'll run the smoke ingest on the 50-sample and confirm that the parser doesn't hit any edge cases. If we see problems, we'll send a short list of rows that need small fixes.

Cheers — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
